description: Add error boundaries to virtual filesystem fallback. Tauri failures silently cascade with no way for UI to know it's in degraded mode. Wrap all Tauri calls in try-catch, expose isVirtualMode() method, emit app event, and show UI warning.
steps: Locate all Tauri API calls: readDir(), readFile(), writeFile(), stat(), etc. in the readTree(), readFile(), writeFile() methods
Wrap each Tauri call in try-catch block with catch that logs error, sets virtualModeReason, and falls back to virtual storage
Add public method isVirtualMode() that returns boolean indicating if using virtual storage
Add property virtualModeReason: string that explains why virtual mode is active (e.g., 'Tauri fs unavailable', 'readDir failed')
Emit an app-level event when falling back to virtual mode (or set a data attribute on document.documentElement, e.g., data-virtual-mode='true')
Update UI/status bar to show a visual warning when isVirtualMode() is true (e.g., badge or icon with tooltip)
Document the fallback chain in detailed JSDoc comments above each method
Add unit test that simulates Tauri failure and verifies fallback behavior
acceptance_criteria: All Tauri failures are caught and logged (no console errors)
isVirtualMode() accurately reflects current storage backend
UI shows clear warning/indicator when in virtual mode
File operations complete successfully even when Tauri unavailable
No unhandled promise rejections during filesystem operations
verification: Manual test: disable Tauri in dev (mock window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ = undefined), verify UI shows virtual mode warning
Verify file operations work in virtual mode (create, read, list)
